hook.line: Every block has its families, and in Bogotá people talk about them by surname: the Garcías upstairs, the Gómez family with the bakery. Spanish does it with one small word and leaves the name alone.

examples.en: The Gómez family has a bakery.

examples.es: Los Torres eran los dueños de la esquina.
examples.en: The Torres family were the owners of the corner shop.
Do you know the Martínez family? (to a friend)

examples.es: La familia López es de Cali.
examples.en: The López family is from Cali.

rule:
To talk about a whole family by its surname, put *los* in front and leave the name exactly as it is: *los García*, *los Gómez*, *los Torres*. English adds an *s* (the Garcías); Spanish never touches the name.

Only *los* tells you it's more than one person, so the verb goes plural: *Los García viven arriba*.

You can also say *la familia García*. That's one family, so the verb stays singular: *La familia García vive arriba*.

In Colombia you'll hear *donde los Rodríguez*: at the Rodríguez family's place.
smallPrint: Surnames in Spanish don't take a plural ending; the article carries the plural for them.

readAndPick.es: El señor Gómez tiene una panadería.
options: The Gómez family has a bakery.
Do you know the Martínez family?

readAndPick.es: La señora López es de Cali.
options: The López family is from Cali.
The Torres family were the owners.

readAndPick.es: Hernando es amigo de los Pérez.
options: Hernando is a friend of the Pérez family.
Hernando is a friend of Mr Pérez.

readAndPick.es: El señor Pérez estuvo en el café.
options: The Pérez family was at the café.
Mr Pérez was at the café.
The Gómez family is from Medellín.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick and type the whole sentence: *___ viven arriba.* (*Los García* or *Los Garcías*) The Garcías live upstairs.
yourTurn.why: The surname never changes; *los* does the plural.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick and type the whole sentence: *La familia García ___ arriba.* (*vive* or *viven*) The García family lives upstairs.
yourTurn.why: *La familia* is one family, so the verb is singular.

yourTurn.prompt: The Gómez family has a bakery. (Use *los*.)
The López family is from Cali. (Use *los*.)
Ask a friend: Do you know the Martínez family? (Use *los*.)
yourTurn.why: Knowing people takes *a*, then *los* and the name as it is.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it the whole family: *El señor Pérez vive en Chapinero.*
yourTurn.why: *El señor* becomes *los*, the name stays, and the verb goes plural.

yourTurn.prompt: Say it with *los* instead: *La familia Torres tiene un carro.*

pitfalls.why: Almost. Spanish doesn't add an *s* to the surname; *los* already says it's the family.
*Los García* is several people, so the verb is plural: *viven*.
The name comes after *familia*, not before it.

personal: Write two sentences about your own family with *los* and your surname: where you live and where you're from.
